source.title: Compositional Abilities Emerge Multiplicatively: Exploring Diffusion Models on a Synthetic Task
source.authors: Maya Okawa; E. Lubana; Robert P. Dick; Hidenori Tanaka

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary information are present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests delayed compositional generalization and multiplicative emergence using diffusion models and attribute probes rather than the original grokking tasks and measures.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the original grokking and mechanistic-interpretability papers, but those citations are not results from this study. It reports its own delayed generalization and compositional-learning results on synthetic images and CelebA. It does not measure training accuracy staying at chance, Fourier circuits, initialization-scale or weight-norm transitions, LLM training, or optimizer/numerical artifacts.
record.test_reason: The study trains conditional diffusion models on synthetic shape images and on CelebA. It reports out-of-distribution compositional generation rising suddenly well after training classes are fit, which the authors call reminiscent of grokking. This is a grokking-like delay on non-algorithmic image data, the first half of V3, measured in a new setting. The delay is on composing new concept combinations, not on held-out examples from the training distribution. The study never varies initialization scale, weight norm or the optimizer.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors frame the results as four failure modes of compositional generalization in diffusion models. Out-of-distribution composition emerges suddenly, in an order set by concept distance, well after the training distribution is fit; they call this reminiscent of grokking and attribute the suddenness to multiplicative reliance on constituent concepts. Underrepresented concepts need far more optimization steps, a critical data-frequency threshold exists, and fine-tuning does not fix misgeneralization. They caution that the results are not definitive for large models.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains conditional diffusion models on synthetic geometric-image concept classes and evaluates generated samples with attribute probes. It does not reproduce the original modular-arithmetic grokking or mechanistic-interpretability methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The timing of generalization varies with concept distance and training-sample frequency; the CelebA results also vary with attribute representation in the data.

fits_no_version.finding: Sudden compositional emergence arises because the accuracy is a product of per-concept accuracies; an additive measure looks smooth. The late bottleneck concept (colour) is itself learned late.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking-like sudden generalization in compositional tasks can stem from multiplicative dependence on constituent skills rather than a hidden gradual circuit.

fits_no_version.finding: A critical number of samples of a concept class (about 10 for colour; an unstated threshold for shape) is needed before the capability to alter that concept appears.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Capability onset in diffusion models has a critical per-concept data-frequency threshold.

record.problems: Most result values relevant here are presented in figures without exact numeric values in the text. The authors caution that the controlled synthetic setup should not be treated as definitive evidence about large generative models. The CelebA experiments are described as partial extensions, and the paper reports an exception to the distance-based sequence.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were omitted.

untested.parts: Entirely: no small algorithmic dataset and no delay-versus-training-set-size curve.
Entirely: no Fourier or other circuit, no measure of memorization removal, no mechanistic progress measure.
Switching the delay on or off via initialization scale or weight norm (lazy-to-rich); no regime manipulation is done.
Entirely: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Entirely: weight decay is fixed at 1e-5; no low-norm efficiency test and no ungrokking.
Entirely: Adam is used throughout and no optimizer or numerical controls are tested.

missing.what: Four-variable concept graph (adds background colour): generalization rises at distance 1, then 2, peaks at 3. Extends the delay sequence.
Replication without global attention: same ordering and delayed emergence of the underrepresented colour that grows with concept distance.
Numeric per-epoch probe accuracies of generated images, giving readable values for the delayed colour acquisition (e.g. 0.0 rising to 0.68 and 0.84).

record.verdict_notes: Grokking is only invoked by analogy, and the measure is out-of-distribution compositional generation, not held-out accuracy on the training distribution, so the V3 link is loose. Training-class fit comes from the generation-accuracy curves, not a training loss. No error bars or multiple seeds are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not use small algorithmic datasets such as modular arithmetic, or report training accuracy saturating while test accuracy remains at chance.

It measures individual concept-prediction progress and compositional performance, but does not identify a Fourier or other mechanistic circuit, measure removal of memorizing components, or test those mechanisms directly.
It reports delayed compositional generalization on synthetic image tasks and CelebA, but does not vary initialization scale or weight norm or test a lazy-to-rich transition.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
The study does not test a low-norm efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking. Weight decay is listed as an optimizer setting, not tested as an explanatory intervention.
The study does not compare identifiable algorithms across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
The study does not test whether optimizer or numerical choices produce or remove the delay.

rows.subject: conditional diffusion model (synthetic concept-graph task; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked generated-image concept-class accuracy over training epochs using linear probes.
rows.measure: Product-based accuracy for generating out-of-distribution concept classes
rows.value: Accuracy begins to rise for concept distance 1 before the distance-2 class; around the 20th epoch, the model learns the underrepresented blue color for a distance-1 class.
rows.note: The paper describes the trajectory in text but gives no exact accuracy value for this condition in the text.
rows.check: Not V2: it measures timing of out-of-distribution generation, not a gradual mechanism. Baseline should be the training-class (lightblue) curves, which rise first.

source_check.correct: Comparison: training-class generation accuracy rises first; distance-1 classes follow, with underrepresented blue generated around epoch 20.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Figure 5 and accompanying text, lines 318–347.
source_check.problem: The text explicitly supplies training-class curves as the earlier-learning comparison.

rows.subject: conditional diffusion model (synthetic concept-graph task; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked generated-image concept-class accuracy over training epochs using linear probes.
rows.measure: Product-based accuracy for generating the out-of-distribution class
rows.value: The model learns the underrepresented color for this class around the 40th epoch, after learning classes nearer to the training set.
rows.note: The text reports the approximate epoch and sequence, not an exact accuracy value.
rows.check: Not V2. Baseline should be training classes fit earlier; distance-2 class 111 jumps around epoch 40.

source_check.correct: Comparison: training classes are learned first, followed by distance-1 classes; distance-2 class 111 acquires blue generation around epoch 40.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Figures 5–6 and accompanying text, lines 318–365.
source_check.problem: The baseline omits the explicitly described earlier learning of training and distance-1 classes.

rows.subject: conditional diffusion model (synthetic concept-graph task; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compared multiplicative and additive measures of compositional performance over training.
rows.baseline: Additive accuracy measure shown for comparison
rows.value: The multiplicative measure shows a sudden improvement; the paper describes the additive measure as suggesting smoother progress.
rows.note: The paper attributes the sudden compositional improvement to the multiplicative influence of constituent concept abilities.
rows.check: The sudden multiplicative-accuracy rise for class 111 is the delayed jump itself (V3). The additive-versus-multiplicative contrast is about how the metric is built, not a circuit or progress measure, so it does not bear on V2; that part goes under fits_no_version.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Figure 6(a) and accompanying text, lines 354–371.

rows.subject: conditional diffusion model (synthetic concept-graph task; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked probe accuracy for each constituent concept over training.
rows.baseline: Random classifier for a concept variable: 0.5
rows.value: The paper reports that strong color-transformation capability is acquired only in the final stage, bottlenecking compositional generalization for class 111.
rows.note: The text describes the temporal pattern but does not provide exact probe accuracies.
rows.check: Per-concept probe dynamics show the colour concept as the bottleneck. Colour is itself acquired late (appendix Fig 14 values near 0, then rising), so it does not show a gradual measure anticipating the jump. No circuit or memorization-removal measure. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: conditional diffusion model (CelebA experiment; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked product-based accuracy for generated attribute combinations during training.
rows.value: Accuracy begins to rise for distance 1, followed by distance 2; the paper says this sequence partially extends its observations to CelebA.
rows.note: The paper notes an exception: node 011, although at distance 1, precedes the memorization stage, which it attributes to gender bias in the training data.
rows.check: Not all CelebA nodes reach 100% accuracy. Node 011 rises before the memorization stage, an exception to the sequence.

source_check.correct: Comparison: training-class memorization curves, shown in blue; distance-1 then distance-2 generalization generally follows, except node 011 precedes memorization. Not all nodes reach 100% within the training time.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, Figure 10(b) and accompanying text, lines 530–543.
source_check.problem: The baseline omits the explicitly identified training-class memorization curves.

rows.subject: conditional diffusion model (CelebA experiment; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compared generation of the more- and less-represented gender attributes over training.
rows.measure: Gender prediction accuracy on generated samples
rows.value: The Female concept class converges faster than the Male concept class because it is more predominant in the dataset.
rows.note: No exact accuracy or epoch values are stated in the text.
rows.check: This is the majority-class comparison curve, not a delayed-generalization result. It should serve as the baseline for R7, not stand as its own row.

rows.subject: conditional diffusion model (CelebA experiment; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compared generation of the more- and less-represented gender attributes over training.
rows.measure: Gender prediction accuracy on generated samples
rows.value: The Male concept class converges more slowly than the Female concept class; the paper identifies Male as underrepresented in the dataset.
rows.note: The paper describes delayed generation of the underrepresented attribute but gives no exact accuracy or epoch values in the text.
rows.check: Baseline should be the Female curve (R6) and training convergence. The underrepresented Male attribute is generated only well after convergence; the text reports it occurs much later as concept distance increases. 'Partial' understated this.

source_check.correct: Comparison: Female curves converge faster than Male curves; Male is underrepresented. Generating underrepresented attributes requires continued training beyond initial training-set convergence.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, Figure 10(c) and accompanying text, lines 543–558.
source_check.problem: The baseline omits the explicit Female comparison and training-set convergence reference.

rows.subject: conditional diffusion model (synthetic concept-graph task; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of training samples from a selected concept class.
rows.value: The model rapidly learns the color concept after being given approximately 10 samples of class 001.
rows.note: The text states the approximate sample count but gives no exact accuracy values.
rows.check: This varies the sample count of one class and measures whether the capability is learned at all, not a delay over training. It is not algorithmic data and no weight decay is involved, so it does not bear on V1 or V5.

rows.value: The model learns the shape concept only after reaching a threshold in the number of class-100 samples; the threshold value is not stated in the text.
rows.note: The figure marks a threshold, but the text does not state its numeric value.
rows.check: Same as R8: a critical-sample threshold, not a delay over training. The threshold value is not stated.

relationships.reason: The delayed sequence holds only partially: not all nodes reach full accuracy, and node 011 precedes memorization. The underrepresented gender attribute is clearly delayed (R5, R7).

relation.reason: The study measures delayed generalization in its own training trajectories, bearing directly on V3's occurrence claim for image data.

tranche.reason: Conditional image diffusion provides a new setting with sudden compositional generalization after training-distribution generation is learned; it does not reproduce the original algorithmic experiment.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v5 dated July 2025, although the record identifies the 2023 conference paper. The reported effect concerns probe-evaluated compositional image generation; it does not establish a lazy-to-rich transition or circuit-level grokking mechanism.

statements.correction: Underrepresented Male generation converges later than Female generation; delay increases with concept distance; controlled synthetic frequency sweeps change compositional accuracy and capability thresholds.
statements.problem: For this study, concept frequency is linked to delayed learning, but R7 does not establish that changing frequency switches the presence of a grokking-like delay on or off.
